items.title: Anne Phillips interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2025
items.q: And then as it went on the newer kids, Al Gorgoni and Trade Martin, the younger kids came in because when all the music started and all of the kids from Brooklyn came in, there’s a different feel to it.

ctx.x: Were the musicians at that time normally able to say — I mean you could say to them, “You know this is in D, can we take it up in E flat it will sound better”? They were capable of that?

Yes. Oh yeah. And usually if they had a guy singer or something that they had to put it in a different key, I have perfect pitch and so it was like having to transpose each note as I sight read it. But the musicians were incredible. Because it was, you know, after the big band era and so the people that were with big bands — Everett Barksdale — do you remember that guitar player with Art Tatum? Everett did a lot of demos. And then as it went on the newer kids, Al Gorgoni and Trade Martin, the younger kids came in…
feel to it. And so the guitar players like Bucky and George and those people didn’t have that feel. So the new young kids were playing it.
